Plain film wrist ___: RIGHT WRIST, FIVE VIEWS.

No acute 
fracture or dislocation is seen.

There are severe degenerative 
changes of the wrist at several joints, but considerably worse 
at the first CMC joint where there is bone-on-bone appearance, 
sclerosis, osteophyte formation, and lateral subluxation.

There 
is minimal soft tissue swelling about the wrist.
IMPRESSION:  No acute fracture or dislocation is identified.

However, in the setting of severe demineralization and 
degenerative change, subtle fracture may be missed.

___ year old male with COPD (on 2L 02 at baseline), dementia, 
recent hospitalization for COPD exacerbation at ___, 
presenting with wrist swelling, fevers, and worsening 
respiratory status, found to have pseudogout, pneumonia, and a 
complicated MDR pseudomonal UTI.

# Complicated MDR pseudomonal UTI: Has a history of chronic 
urinary obstruction and uses intermittent straight caths.
Initially presented to ___ and was transferred to ___.

Found incidentally on UA to have bacteruria, with subsequent 
foley revealing the infection.

Only intermediately sensitive to 
ceftaz, cefepime, and amikacin, and sensitive to zosyn.

He was 
started on a 10 day course of IV cefepime 2g q12hrs (infused 
over 3 hours to keep  above MIC) per the recommendations of the 
infectious disease team.

Initially he appeared somewhat 
uroseptic with soft BPs and low urine output but responded well 
to IVF boluses and cefepime.

His foley was removed out of 
concern for being a nidus of infection and he was intermittently 
straight cathed per his home regimen.

He had a repeat UA after 
starting antiobiotics which was much improved and showed 
resolving infection.

At discharge, a mid-line IV access line was 
placed for his cefepime course, which will end on ___.

In the 
future, it would be preferable to avoid placing foleys in his 
bladder and instead use straight cathing given the severity of 
this UTI.

# Pseudogout: On presentation he was found to have significant 
bilateral wrist pain and swelling.

Wrist tap showed a crystal 
arthropathy consistent with CPPD.

Joint fluid cultures were 
negative for septic arthritis.

Initially he was managed with 
indomethacin but developed some mild ___ and ___ this was 
switched to colchicine (___ompleting on ___ as well 
as intermittent ice to the wrists at the suggestion of the 
rheumatology team.

PO steroids were withheld given his ongoing 
systemic infection.
He was given pain control with oxycodone and

The swelling and pain in the wrists improved slowly 
throughout the admission.

# HCAP: Presented with worsening respiratory status and found to 
have a RLL infiltrate seen on chest imaging, in the setting of 
baseline CHF.

Respiratory status improved back to baseline with 
nebs and antibiotics.

Initially treated with vanc/cipro/azithro, 
then narrowed to levaquin, and then broadened back to cefepime 
given concomitant treatment of complicated UTI.

Initially there 
was some concern that he might have been aspirating given 
location of the infiltrate but speech and swallow was consulted 
and they did not see any obvious evidence of aspiration at the 
bedside.

# Confusion: Was intermittently confused at night in a waxing 
and waning fashion.

This was felt to be mild delirium, 
multifactorial: systemic infection and pain in the setting of 
hospitalization and baseline mild dementia.

He was given pain 
control, frequent reorientation, avoidance of deliriogenic meds, 
and his foley was removed.
# Hypoalbuminemia: At presentation, the patient had an elevated

INR and low albumin, which was suggestive of poor nutritional 
status.
# Hypertension: His home amlodipine was continued.

His labetalol 
was briefly held in the setting of urosepsis and soft pressures, 
but was restarted at discharge.
# Chronic pain: Continued his fentanyl patch.
# Psych: His lorazepam and mirtazapine were continued.
# GERD: His home omeprazole was continued.
